issues.title: Functional API: parallel @task interrupts are pending but invoke/get_state surface only one
issues.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

With the Functional API (`@entrypoint` + `@task`), parallel tasks that each call `interrupt()` leave **multiple** INTERRUPT writes on the checkpointer, but `invoke` / `get_state().interrupts` surface **only one**.

Scalar `Command(resume=...)` then fails with:

`When there are multiple pending interrupts, you must specify the interrupt id when resuming.`

…which proves multiples exist — but the public API never exposed the other ids, so callers cannot build a complete `Command(resume={id: value})` map.

Contrast: the same fan-out via `Send` on a `StateGraph` correctly surfaces all parallel interrupts.

Distinct from closed #6624/#6625 (ToolNode aggregation) and open #8579 (scalar resume wrongly accepted for multi-interrupt subgraph tasks — opposite symptom).

### To Reproduce

```python
from langgraph.func import entrypoint, task
from langgraph.types import interrupt, Command
from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import InMemorySaver

@task
def ask(q: int):
    return interrupt({\"q\": q})

@entrypoint(checkpointer=InMemorySaver())
def workflow(n: int):
    futs = [ask(i) for i in range(n)]
    return [f.result() for f in futs]

cfg = {\"configurable\": {\"thread_id\": \"t1\"}}
out = workflow.invoke(3, cfg)
print(out[\"__interrupt__\"])          # only 1 surfaced
print(workflow.get_state(cfg).interrupts)  # only 1
workflow.invoke(Command(resume=\"x\"), cfg)
# RuntimeError: multiple pending interrupts — must specify interrupt id
```

Full offline repro script available on request.

### Expected behavior

All parallel `@task` interrupts should appear in `__interrupt__` / `get_state().interrupts` (with ids), matching StateGraph+`Send` behavior.

### Environment

- `langgraph==1.2.12`
- Python 3.13

issues.title: Clarify that durability modes do not imply exactly-once external side effects
issues.body_excerpt:
### Checked other resources

- [x] I used GitHub search and found #8039 as the relevant underlying crash/recovery discussion.
- [x] This request is narrower than changing runtime semantics: it is a documentation/API-contract clarification.
- [x] I am not proposing a LangGraph idempotency or exactly-once mechanism.

### Problem

The public `Durability` docstrings currently describe only graph/checkpoint persistence timing:

- `sync`: persist before the next step
- `async`: persist while the next step executes
- `exit`: persist when the graph exits

That wording can be read more strongly than LangGraph guarantees for user code with consequential external side effects.

As established in #8039, even if checkpoint/write ordering is deterministic, a node or tool can:

```text
external effect commits
→ process crashes / acknowledgement is lost
→ graph completion evidence is not durably available
→ recovery re-executes node/tool code
```

So graph/checkpoint durability and exactly-once external-effect execution are separate guarantees.

### Proposed documentation clarification

Add a short note to the core and Python SDK `Durability` docstrings:

- durability controls persistence timing for LangGraph state/checkpoints;
- it does not provide exactly-once semantics for external side effects performed by node/tool code;
- applications that need bounded effect multiplicity should use stable logical operation identity at the external-effect boundary and reconcile an ambiguous outcome before retrying.

No new API or retry mechanism is proposed.

### Existing patch

I prepared a docs-only patch in #9239. It was automatically closed by the external-contribution gate because it did not first link to an approved/assigned issue. I am opening this issue to follow that process rather than bypass it.

If maintainers agree this clarification belongs in the public `Durability` contract, I can re-link #9239 after approval/assignment.

issues.title: Feature Request: Compensatory Rollback Journals & Blast-Radius Containment for ToolNode
issues.body_excerpt:
### Motivation
When deploying LangGraph workflows to manage cloud infrastructure, network routing, or database operations, errors or invariant breaches at step k currently leave earlier mutations live in production without automated compensatory undo semantics:
`[A_1, A_2, ..., A_k] => [A_k^-1, ..., A_2^-1, A_1^-1]`

### Proposed Solution
Add `TransactionalToolNode` and `CompensatoryJournal` to `langgraph.prebuilt`.
1. Records mutating tool actions to an in-memory LIFO journal.
2. Supports generating exact reverse compensatory DAGs via `.rollback_all()` upon unhandled exceptions or invariant breaches.
3. Provides pre-execution blast-radius containment (`max_blast_radius`) and blocks unauthorized destructive commands.

We have a zero-dependency implementation ready with tests in PR #9249.

issues.title: [Feature] Add safe prune support to Postgres checkpoint savers
issues.body_excerpt:
### Privileged issue

- [ ] I am a LangGraph maintainer.

### Issue Content

Opening this issue following a recommendation from a LangChain Expert in the Forum discussion:

- https://forum.langchain.com/t/proposal-add-safe-keep-latest-pruning-to-postgressaver/4291

## Problem

`BaseCheckpointSaver` exposes `prune` / `aprune`, but `PostgresSaver` and `AsyncPostgresSaver` do not currently implement them.

Applications using the open-source Postgres checkpointer directly can therefore accumulate an unbounded number of rows in:

- `checkpoints`
- `checkpoint_writes`
- `checkpoint_blobs`

Application-level message trimming may reduce the size of the current state, and `DeltaChannel` may reduce repeated payload storage, but neither mechanism limits the number of checkpoint records retained for a long-lived thread.

## Related work

PR #6883 already proposes Postgres implementations of several extended saver methods, including `prune`:

- https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/pull/6883

Its `keep_latest` implementation retains the newest database checkpoint per thread and namespace. However, a `DeltaChannel` value may depend on an earlier snapshot seed, ancestor checkpoints, and intervening checkpoint writes. Removing every ancestor while retaining only the newest row can therefore make the retained state unrecoverable.

## Proposed phase-one scope

Implement `prune` and `aprune` for:

- `PostgresSaver`
- `AsyncPostgresSaver`

Support the existing `delete` and `keep_latest` strategies.

### `delete`

For the requested thread IDs:

- Delete all checkpoints, checkpoint writes, and checkpoint blobs.
- Preserve data belonging to unrelated threads.
- Allow complete deletion of threads containing `DeltaChannel` state, because no retained state needs to remain recoverable.

### `keep_latest`

For ordinary checkpoints:

- Retain the latest checkpoint for each `(thread_id, checkpoint_ns)`.
- Preserve the writes and blobs required to load and resume the retained state.
- Remove older checkpoints and unreferenced writes and blobs.
- Preserve unrelated threads and namespaces.
- Perform validation and deletion in one transaction.

After pruning, the retained checkpoint must remain readable through `get_tuple()` / `aget_tuple()`, and graph execution must be able to continue from it.

## DeltaChannel safety

This deliberately follows the third safe option documented on `BaseCheckpointSaver.prune`: skip pruning threads that use `DeltaChannel` until dependency-aware pruning i

The server accepts the full list when it is sent as one JSON-encoded query value, for example `stream_mode=["values","messages-tuple","custom"]`. Could the SDK serialize sequences in that format, or could the server accept repeated query parameters?

```python
from typing import TypedDict

from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import InMemorySaver
from langgraph.graph import START, StateGraph


class State(TypedDict, total=False):
    notes: dict
    done: bool


class FlakySaver(InMemorySaver):
    def put(self, config, checkpoint, metadata, new_versions):
        if metadata["step"] == 1:  # the save after `research` fails once, like a DB timeout
            raise ConnectionError("checkpoint save failed")
        return super().put(config, checkpoint, metadata, new_versions)


graph = (
    StateGraph(State)
    .add_node("research", lambda s: {"notes": {"x": 1}})
    .add_node("write", lambda s: {"done": True})
    .add_edge(START, "research")
    .add_edge("research", "write")
    .compile(checkpointer=FlakySaver())
)
config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "1"}}
try:
    graph.invoke({}, config)  # default durability="async"
except ConnectionError:
    pass
# expect notes in the saved state; notes is gone
print(graph.get_state(config).values)
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```shell

```

### Description

- With the default `durability="async"`, the checkpoint save after `research` fails once.
- I expected `invoke` to raise and the thread to keep `notes`, as it does with `durability="sync"`.
- Instead `notes` is gone from the thread for good, while the later `done` is saved.

```
{'done': True}

`_checkpointer_put_after_previous` in `pregel/_loop.py` saves the next checkpoint in a `finally` even when the previous save failed, so `notes` is never written. Also reproduces on `PostgresSaver` with a real lock timeout.

issues.title: Same-named local packages collide in generated Dockerfiles and runtime paths
issues.body_excerpt:
### Checked other resources

- [x] This is a reproducible LangGraph bug, not a usage question or a langchain-community issue.
- [x] Searched existing issues and PRs and did not find the same problem.
- [x] Reproduced with the latest stable version of the affected package and current main.
- [x] Included a self-contained reproduction below.

### Description

Generating a Dockerfile for an application with distinct local Python packages that share a directory name can silently omit a package. Three real packages named `shared` receive destinations `shared`, `shared_1`, and `shared_1`; for external dependencies the third build context exists but the Dockerfile copies the second one twice.

Even two same-named packages can receive incorrect graph or runtime-hook paths because those references use the directory basename instead of the allocated destination name.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

This generates the Dockerfile without building an image or contacting a remote service.

```python
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from langgraph_cli.config import config_to_docker, validate_config

with TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
    root = Path(temporary)
    project = root / "app"
    project.mkdir()
    config_path = project / "langgraph.json"
    config_path.write_text("{}", encoding="utf-8")
    (project / "agent.py").write_text("graph = None", encoding="utf-8")
    dependencies = ["."]
    for number in range(3):
        package = root / f"team{number}" / "shared"
        package.mkdir(parents=True)
        (package / "pyproject.toml").write_text(
            f'[project]\nname = "team{number}-shared"\nversion = "0.0.1"\n',
            encoding="utf-8",
        )
        dependencies.append(f"../team{number}/shared")
    config = validate_config({"dependencies": dependencies, "graphs": {"agent": "./agent.py:graph"}})
    dockerfile, contexts = config_to_docker(config_path, config, base_image="langchain/langgraph-api")
    print(contexts)
    print("\n".join(line for line in dockerfile.splitlines() if line.startswith("COPY --from=")))
```

Observed: contexts `shared`, `shared_1`, and `shared_1_1` exist, but the COPY instructions use `shared`, `shared_1`, and `shared_1`. The third package is missing from those instructions.

The WHATWG SSE example explicitly states that an empty ID resets the last event ID and that the next reconnect should omit the header: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html#event-stream-interpretation .

issues.title: Synchronous SSE errors leave responses open and exhaust the HTTP connection pool
issues.body_excerpt:
### Checked other resources

- [x] This is a reproducible LangGraph bug, not a usage question or a langchain-community issue.
- [x] Searched existing issues and PRs and did not find the same problem.
- [x] Reproduced with the latest stable version of the affected package and current main.
- [x] Included a self-contained reproduction below.

### Description

A failed synchronous SSE handshake leaves its streaming HTTP response open. Repeated 4xx/5xx handshakes can exhaust the shared client's connection pool, preventing subsequent requests even after the thread stream context exits.

`SyncProtocolSseTransport.open_event_stream()` raises from `raise_for_status()` before registering the response for cleanup, so `transport.close()` cannot release it. The async transport already closes failed responses.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

```python
import httpx
from langgraph_sdk.stream.transport.sync_http import SyncProtocolSseTransport

def respond(request):
    return httpx.Response(503, stream=httpx.ByteStream(b"unavailable"))

with httpx.Client(base_url="http://test", transport=httpx.MockTransport(respond)) as client:
    transport = SyncProtocolSseTransport(client=client, thread_id="thread")
    try:
        transport.open_event_stream({"channels": ["values"]})
    except httpx.HTTPStatusError as error:
        response = error.response
    transport.close()
    print(response.is_closed)  # False; expected True
```

### Observed / expected result

Observed: `False`. Expected: `True`; the error response should be closed before propagating the HTTP error.

Also reproduced through the public `SyncLangGraphClient.threads.stream()` API against a localhost HTTP/1.1 server: with `max_connections=1`, a 503 handshake followed by exiting the stream context makes `threads.get()` raise `httpx.PoolTimeout`. Closing the failed response restores that next request. The small pool exposes the leak after one failure; no remote service or API key is required.

### Proposed fix and validation

[Prepared change and regression tests](https://github.com/bnkaiteam/langgraph/commit/d5a1d7672e26048955f2059adde03226b9c3a957): close the response when HTTP status validation fails, then re-raise the original error. Five regression cases cover 401/429/500/503, actual stream closure, and a successful handshake after a failure. Successful responses retain their normal lifetime.

issues.title: SqliteSaver.list() blocks checkpoint writes while synchronous history iteration is paused
issues.body_excerpt:
### Checked other resources

- [x] This is a bug, not a usage question.
- [x] I added a clear and descriptive title.
- [x] I searched GitHub; #8558 is related but covers the async saver.
- [x] Reproduced with LangGraph's public checkpoint APIs on current main.
- [x] This is not related to langchain-community.
- [x] The example below runs as-is without a model or external service.

### Related Issues / PRs

#8558 reports the async counterpart. The retrieved diff for #8562 changes only `aio.py`; this report concerns synchronous `SqliteSaver.list()`.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

```python
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from contextlib import closing

from langgraph.checkpoint.base import empty_checkpoint
from langgraph.checkpoint.sqlite import SqliteSaver

config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "sync-history", "checkpoint_ns": ""}}

with (
    SqliteSaver.from_conn_string(":memory:") as saver,
    ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1) as pool,
):
    stored = saver.put(config, empty_checkpoint(), {}, {})
    with closing(saver.list(stored)) as history:
        next(history)
        pool.submit(
            saver.put, stored, empty_checkpoint(), {}, {}
        ).result(timeout=3)
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace

`concurrent.futures.TimeoutError` at `result(timeout=3)`. Iterator cleanup releases the lock before the executor joins its worker, so the example exits rather than leaving a blocked process.

### Description

I expect to be able to persist a new checkpoint while inspecting an existing checkpoint from history. Instead, `list()` holds the saver's non-reentrant lock across its yield, and the write cannot complete until the iterator advances or closes. Calling another saver operation on the consumer's own thread can therefore deadlock.

Reproduced on upstream main at `87f1c8eb9a99ca701d294b3b83cac02c935ebe92`. I prepared a synchronous-only fix that reads serialized checkpoint rows and pending writes under the existing lock, closes both cursors, and releases the lock before yielding. Deserialization stays lazy, so a corrupt older checkpoint does not prevent reading a valid newer checkpoint first. Matching serialized rows are buffered; `limit` bounds memory use.

Four test cases cover paused writes on memory/file databases, pending-write consistency after concurrent changes, and lazy deserialization. Three fail on the unmodified source and all four pass with the fix. Local formatting, lint/type checks and the packag

issues.title: Python SDK loses the first SSE event type when the stream starts with a UTF-8 BOM
issues.body_excerpt:
### Checked other resources

- [x] This is a bug report, not a usage question.
- [x] The title describes the issue.
- [x] I searched existing issues and PRs for BOM / byte order mark and found no matching report or fix.
- [x] The reproduction isolates the SDK's SSE decoding behavior.
- [x] Reproduced on the latest stable integration package, `langgraph-sdk==0.4.6`.
- [x] This is not related to langchain-community.
- [x] The example below is self-contained.

### Description

A leading UTF-8 BOM changes the first event type from `values` to an empty string in Python `client.runs.stream()`; the JSON payload is unchanged. Both sync and async clients reproduce this on 0.4.6 and the `main` source snapshot checked on 2026-10-07.

This is a local protocol compatibility test, **not an observed production incident or a test against a deployed LangGraph server**. A local HTTP server emitting `text.encode("utf-8-sig")` also reproduces it through the public sync/async client factories, without a mock transport.

The WHATWG SSE rules use UTF-8 decode, which strips one leading BOM: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html#event-stream-interpretation .

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

Install `langgraph-sdk==0.4.6`, then run:

```python
import httpx
from langgraph_sdk.client import SyncLangGraphClient

def read(payload):
    transport = httpx.MockTransport(lambda request: httpx.Response(
        200, headers={"Content-Type": "text/event-stream"}, content=payload
    ))
    with httpx.Client(transport=transport, base_url="https://example.invalid") as http:
        return list(SyncLangGraphClient(http).runs.stream(None, "agent", version="v1"))

payload = b'event: values\ndata: {"step": 1}\n\n'
print(read(payload))
print(read(b"\xef\xbb\xbf" + payload))
```

Expected: both return `StreamPart(event='values', data={'step': 1}, id=None)`.

Actual: the second returns `StreamPart(event='', data={'step': 1}, id=None)`.

### Validation and proposed scope

Six sync/async regression cases: four BOM cases fail, two no-BOM controls pass, including a BOM split across three HTTP chunks. The existing source `tests/test_client_stream.py` suite passes (14 tests).

Proposed scope: ignore one BOM only at the start of each SSE stream; preserve later BOM characters and unrelated parsing behavior.

Would you consider this compatibility scenario worth fixing? If so, please confirm the preferred fix location and assign this issue to `Ra1nhy` before I open a co

### Related Issues / PRs

Same codec, already-reported symptoms: #8705 (numpy scalars), #8689 (C-contiguous datetime64/timedelta64).

The three defects below are distinct from those two and, as far as I can tell, unreported. All five share one root cause: `EXT_NUMPY_ARRAY` describes an array with `dtype.str` plus a raw buffer, and that pair cannot represent every array.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

```python
import numpy as np
from langgraph.checkpoint.serde.jsonplus import JsonPlusSerializer

serde = JsonPlusSerializer()

# 1. Structured dtypes decode as opaque void bytes -- no error raised.
arr = np.array([(1, 2.0), (3, 4.0)], dtype=[("a", "i4"), ("b", "f8")])
out = serde.loads_typed(serde.dumps_typed(arr))
print("1. structured in :", arr.dtype, arr.tolist())
print("1. structured out:", out.dtype, out.tolist())

# 2. Object arrays persist raw CPython pointers, then decode to None.
obj = np.array([{"a": 1}, {"b": 2}], dtype=object)
payload = serde.dumps_typed(obj)[1]
pointers = b"".join(int(id(x)).to_bytes(8, "little") for x in obj)
print("2. id() bytes present in checkpoint payload:", pointers in payload)
print("2. object array decodes to:", serde.loads_typed(serde.dumps_typed(obj)))

# 3. Round-tripped arrays are read-only.
a = np.arange(6, dtype=np.float64).reshape(2, 3)
r = serde.loads_typed(serde.dumps_typed(a))
print("3. writeable:", r.flags.writeable)
try:
    r[0, 0] = 99.0
except ValueError as e:
    print("3. in-place update raises:", type(e).__name__, e)
```

issues.title: Docs safety guidance: auditable final-state receipts for agent completion claims?
issues.body_excerpt:
Hi, I maintain SACP, a small text-first receipt layer for AI agent work:
https://github.com/aDragon0707/sacp

I noticed LangGraph emphasizes durable execution, human-in-the-loop review, stateful agents, and long-running workflows. That seems like a natural place for guidance on auditable final-state receipts.

I also saw that this repo's `examples/` directory is archived and points users to the consolidated LangChain docs, so I am opening an issue instead of sending a docs PR to the wrong place.

Would LangGraph docs accept a small safety-oriented section or example about final completion receipts?

The pattern would document:

- what the agent claimed
- what evidence supports each claim
- who owns the next step
- whether human approval is required before publishing, deploying, writing memory, or taking another external action

Concrete failure mode:

```text
Done. All tests passed. Ready to publish.
```

This final output contains completion, test, and external-action claims, but it may not attach command output, trace evidence, or human approval.

No runtime dependency, no behavior change, and no framework replacement. The goal is just safety guidance for auditing final agent state.

issues.title: Checkpoint saved at an interrupt_after pause is never emitted on the checkpoints / debug stream
issues.body_excerpt:
### Checked other resources

- [x] This is a bug, not a usage question.
- [x] I added a clear and descriptive title that summarizes this issue.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [x] I am sure that this is a bug in LangGraph rather than my code.
- [x] The bug is not resolved by updating to the latest stable version of LangGraph (or the specific integration package).
- [x] This is not related to the langchain-community package.
- [x] I posted a self-contained, minimal, reproducible example. A maintainer can copy it and run it AS IS.

### Related Issues / PRs

None found.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

```python
import operator
from typing import Annotated, TypedDict

from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import InMemorySaver
from langgraph.graph import END, START, StateGraph


class State(TypedDict):
    messages: Annotated[list[str], operator.add]


builder = StateGraph(State)
builder.add_node("one", lambda s: {"messages": ["one"]})
builder.add_node("two", lambda s: {"messages": ["two"]})
builder.add_edge(START, "one")
builder.add_edge("one", "two")
builder.add_edge("two", END)
graph = builder.compile(checkpointer=InMemorySaver(), interrupt_after=["one"])

config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "1"}}
streamed = [
    (c["metadata"]["step"], c["next"])
    for c in graph.stream({"messages": []}, config, stream_mode="checkpoints")
]
head = graph.get_state(config)
print("streamed checkpoints (step, next):", streamed)
print("saved head checkpoint (step, next):", (head.metadata["step"], list(head.next)))
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```shell
streamed checkpoints (step, next): [(-1, ['__start__']), (0, ['one'])]
saved head checkpoint (step, next): (1, ['two'])
```

### Description

When a graph pauses because of `interrupt_after`, the checkpoint saved at the pause (step 1 above, `next == ['two']`) is never emitted on `stream_mode="checkpoints"`, nor as a `checkpoint` event on `stream_mode="debug"`. The last checkpoint the stream reports is the one from before node `one` ran. A client that tracks checkpoint ids from the stream and resumes from the last one it saw runs `one` again.

`interrupt_before` does not have this problem: the paused checkpoint shows up on the stream.

The checkpoint event is only produced at the start of the next `tick()` (`libs/langgraph/langgraph/pregel/_loop.py:641-642`). `after_tick()` saves the checkpoint (`:743`) and then raises `GraphInterrupt` for
